pw_slow_hash.note: Uses PBKDF2-SHA256 with 200,000 iterations and a random 16-byte salt from secrets.token_bytes(16) (app.py:58).

token_csprng.note: Session tokens are 256-bit values from the secrets module. Only a SHA-256 hash of each token is stored (app.py:196).

no_hardcoded_secret.note: There is no signing key or secret in the code. Tokens are random values looked up in the database, not signed.

token_expiry.evidence: app.py:113 SELECT user_id FROM sessions WHERE token_hash = ?
token_expiry.note: The sessions table has a created_at column, but the token lookup never checks it. Tokens stay valid forever.

logout_revokes.note: Logout only clears the token in the browser. The server has no logout endpoint and never deletes from sessions.

owner_checks.evidence: app.py:165 WHERE id=? AND user_id=?; app.py:236 UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND user_id=?; app.py:251 DELETE FROM notes WHERE id=? AND user_id=?; app.py:213 SELECT 1 FROM notes WHERE id=? AND user_id=?
owner_checks.note: Read, update, delete and share are all limited to the note's owner.

share_token_strong.note: 24 random bytes from the secrets module is 192 bits, above the 128-bit minimum.

login_rate_limit.evidence: app.py:193 if not user or not password_ok(password, user["password_hash"]): return self.error("Invalid email or password", 401)
login_rate_limit.note: Failed logins are not counted, slowed down or locked out.

password_policy.evidence: app.py:181 if not isinstance(password, str) or len(password) < 8:
password_policy.note: The server rejects passwords shorter than 8 characters at signup.

sql_parameterized.note: Every query that includes user input uses ? placeholders. No query is built with string formatting.

xss_safe_render.note: The page escapes titles and bodies with esc() (index.html:25), which covers & < > ' ". The server-rendered shared page also escapes them with html.escape (app.py:139-140).

security_headers.note: No response sets Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options or X-Frame-Options.
